We use two complementary preparations: Grover-type amplitude amplification to redistribute probability toward a specified target, and oracle-free shallow circuits to shape the distribution at low depth. Zero-time benchmarks combine noiseless simulations with finite-shot sampling and IBM Quantum demonstrations on up to 20 qubits. Sector statistics distinguish low occupation from cancellation within an occupied sector, while comparisons with noiseless simulations show that characteristic features of the engineered cumulative patterns persist on hardware. We also extend the analysis to multi-qubit diagonal observables and connect their sign and sector rules to explicit preparation choices. These results provide a basis for designing and assessing structured ensembles through their operator-resolved contributions to quantum correlation measurements.
item.dc:creator: Myeongsu Kim, Manas Sajjan, Sabre Kais

item.title: Physics inspired quantum algorithm for QCD splitting functions
item.description: arXiv:2605.06789v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a modular quantum circuit primitive to model entanglement dynamics in QCD parton splitting and use it as a composable building block for data-driven, physics-consistent modelling of parton-shower kinematics. For the pure-gluon channel, we derive an analytic expression for the helicity entanglement generated at the splitting vertex, quantified via the concurrence, and construct a two-qubit circuit whose $\sigma_3$ expectation values encode the momentum shared between outgoing gluons. The circuit reproduces the QCD-predicted concurrence by construction, which fixes a two-qubit correlator that the momentum fractions alone do not determine. Iterating the primitive, the concurrence obeys a product rule across successive splittings. Calibrating the circuit parameters to LHC jet substructure data relates the reconstructed momentum-sharing fractions directly to circuit rotation angles. Composing multiple splitting primitives yields multi-prong momentum-fraction distributions; we compare the three- and four-prong cases against experimental data, reproducing the core of the distributions. For the three-prong configuration, we execute the circuit on superconducting quantum hardware, recover the momentum-fraction distributions after a device-bias correction calibrated on a held-out subset, and study how noise alters the entanglement-dependent observable. This work provides a concrete framework for quantum-native parton-shower modules that encode quantum correlations at the level of splitting dynamics, and offers physics-informed ans\"atze for future quantum algorithms for QCD.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Rouxinol, Yacine Haddad, Cenk T\"uys\"uz, Sofia Vallecorsa, Michele Grossi

item.title: Degree-Guided Adiabatic Quantum Algorithm for MIS with Neutral Atoms
item.description: arXiv:2605.16944v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a quantum adiabatic algorithm for solving MIS with Rydberg atoms, which uses graph degrees to engineer the Hamiltonian for adiabatic evolution. Our approach extends the algorithm of Pichler et al. for MIS state preparation, which uses time-dependent global controls to excite atoms while the Rydberg blockade mechanism suppresses adjacent excitations. To accelerate adiabatic evolution, we introduce local light shifts that favor excitation of low-degree nodes and constrain the final Hamiltonian so that energy scales inversely with the number of Rydberg excitations, preventing convergence to non-MIS states. Benchmarking our degree-dependent MIS algorithm with the traditional adiabatic algorithm on a set of 1000 MIS instances, we demonstrate numerically that our algorithm inflates the minimal spectral gap and, consequently, accelerates the convergence. By fitting power-law relations for both the time-to-solution and success probability metrics as a function of the hardness parameter, we demonstrate a superior scaling exponent for our algorithm over the traditional global protocol. Furthermore, the classical Hamiltonian engineering step required to construct degree-dependent controls introduces only polynomial overhead. These results indicate that our algorithm can be used to extend the size of graphs for which MIS can be found on physical hardware. Moreover, our approach extends beyond MIS to additional graph problems such as MAX-CUT.
item.dc:creator: Guy Karni, Noam Cohen, Adi Pick

item.title: Quantum Quenches that Resemble Operator Growth
item.description:
arXiv:2605.23874v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study growth quenches, which are local quenches that may gradually destabilize a false vacuum in certain kinetic constrained quantum lattice models, such as the East-West model. We point out a formal analogy with the dynamics of a local operator in the Heisenberg picture. Exploiting this analogy, we obtain several results on growth quenches by adapting operator-dynamics concepts and methods. First, applying the Krylov approach (recursion method), we conjecture the linear growth of Lanzcos coefficients in generic quenches, $a_m \sim 
u m$ (diagonal), and $b_m \sim \alpha m$ (off-diagonal), extending an operator growth hypothesis. We show that the growth quench dynamics is localized in both Krylov and Fock spaces when $|
u| > 2 \alpha$, and derive a bound for the growth quench analogue of Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L \le \sqrt{4 \alpha^2 - 
u^2}$ when $|
u| < 2 \alpha$. Second, we realize the Fock localization in large $N$ solvable growth quenches inspired by Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) models. The bound on Lyapunov exponent is saturated in large-$q$ SYK grow quench. By contrast, the growth quench is almost always Fock localized in a nonrandom all-to-all growth quench amenable to semiclassics. Finally, in the 1D East-West model, we interpret Fock space cage states as the existence of a conserved charge. We show that the latter has ballistic transport due to current conservation. Moreover, adding hopping with a fine-tuned amplitude induces a partial localization due to a flat band. Our work suggest growth quenches as a promising approach to realize non-equilibrium coherent phenomena in many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Cao

item.title: Sideband fingerprints of antibunched light in cascaded quantum wave mixing
item.description: arXiv:2605.25828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum wave mixing on a single superconducting qubit produces a hierarchy of coherent side peaks associated with elastic multiphoton scattering pathways. In a cascaded source--probe geometry these pathways become sensitive to the photon statistics of the radiation emitted by the source qubit. We develop an analytical theory of this effect starting from the cascaded master equation in the weak-driving regime. In the coherent-filtering limit when the decay rate of the probe qubit is less than that of the source, the standard coherent--coherent wave-mixing hierarchy is recovered. In the opposite limit, side peaks associated with multiphoton absorption from the antibunched source field are parametrically suppressed. Numerical solutions confirm the analytical scaling laws. The resulting sideband hierarchy provides a frequency-domain fingerprint of antibunched itinerant microwave light.
item.dc:creator: R. D. Ivanovskikh, W. V. Pogosov, A. A. Elistratov, A. Yu. Dmitriev, T. R. Sabirov, A. V. Vasenin, S. A. Gunin, O. V. Astafiev

item.title: Quantum geometry of connected state manifolds: When diabolic points act as bridges between eigenstate manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2605.28351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric Hamiltonians often exhibit point-like spectral degeneracies, called diabolic points (DPs) or conical intersections, which can lead to singularities in the Provost-Vallee metric of eigenstate manifolds. We regularise the metric by a transformation to polar coordinates and develop a formalism in which DPs act as bridges between adjacent eigenstate manifolds, glueing them into a single connected state manifold (CSM). We characterise the topology of this structure and extend the local rules for nodal lines governing the Berry phase to global ones. On the CSM, the class of geodesics can be enlarged by those passing through the DPs. They can be stable with respect to their initial direction, and can be shorter than those constrained to a single eigenstate manifold, providing new geodesic shortcuts. Further, the CSM provides a new mechanism for Berry phase computation along paths traversing the DPs.
item.dc:creator: Jan St\v{r}ele\v{c}ek, Jakub Novotn\'y, Pavel Cejnar

item.title: How To Track Qubits Through Space and Time (Or: Sailing in a Quantum Boat)
item.description: arXiv:2605.30732v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While quantum position verification aims to certify a prover's location using quantum information, existing security definitions only guarantee that part of the successful adversarial party is in the claimed location. This leaves open the possibility that a distributed team of adversaries can jointly simulate a prover in a way that defeats the intended meaning of `being at a location' in position-based cryptography. We introduce stronger notions of position verification that we call quantum localization, which requires that there is a specified, unclonable state at the verified spacetime point-and that this state can be found nowhere else. We show that quantum localization leads naturally to a meaningful notion of trajectory verification, in which quantum information is verifiably tracked through space and time. We construct quantum localization and trajectory verification protocols using quantum anchor states, which generalize coset states from unclonable cryptography. The security of our schemes is proven in the classical oracle (i.e. ideal obfuscation) model, which can be heuristically instantiated in the plain model using post-quantum indistinguishability obfuscation. We also introduce and instantiate the concept of functionality localization, which guarantees that the adversary has the ability to compute a secret function at the verified spacetime point, and this function cannot be computed anywhere else. This raises the intriguing possibility of localizing computational capabilities in space and time. More broadly, we believe our notions of quantum localization and subsequent feasibility results provide stronger foundations for position-based cryptography. At a conceptual level, our results also explore the tight link between two fundamental notions in physics-location and information-thus serving as a natural foundation for cryptographic capabilities tied to physical spacetime.
item.dc:creator: James Bartusek, Zikuan Huang, Leo Orshansky, Henry Yuen

item.title: Counterdiabatic Raman Atom Optics for Compact High-Sensitivity Gravimetry
item.description: arXiv:2606.16945v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large-momentum-transfer (LMT) atom interferometry provides a route toward enhanced inertial sensitivity in compact quantum sensors, but its scalability is limited by the accumulation of pulse-transfer errors across long Raman pulse sequences. We investigate theoretically the use of stimulated Raman shortcut-to-adiabatic passage (STIRSAP) for high-fidelity LMT atom optics in a Mach--Zehnder interferometer geometry. The counterdiabatic correction is encoded directly into the Raman pulse envelopes, eliminating the need for auxiliary microwave or radio-frequency control fields. Numerical simulations based on an effective Raman model show that $1~\mu\mathrm{s}$ STIRSAP pulses achieve single-pulse transfer fidelities of $F_\pi = 0.99902$ while maintaining negligible pulse-time overhead even at high momentum order. We analyze the resulting tradeoff between interferometric phase enhancement and compound contrast decay and identify an unconstrained shot-noise optimum near $n\approx270$. The analysis further shows that practical operation at extreme LMT order is constrained by wave-packet separation, vibration noise, Doppler detuning, and accumulated systematic effects rather than by pulse duration itself. These results establish superadiabatic Raman control as a promising approach for scalable high-fidelity atom optics and clarify the physical limitations governing compact high-order atom interferometers.
item.dc:creator: Asad Ali, Hamid Arian Zad, Saif Al-Kuwari, Muhammad Irtiza Hussain, Muhammad Talha Rahim, Hashir Kuniyil, Tim Byrnes, James Q. Quach, Saeed Haddadi

item.title: Estimating the concurrence for quantum states via symmetric measurements
item.description: arXiv:2606.31010v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Concurrence is one of the most well-known entanglement measures. We show that, for arbitrary bipartite states, the lower bound of concurrence induced by symmetric measurements is always tighter than the one obtain from realignment. Besides, we derive an extended version of lower bound of concurrence induced by symmetric measurements, which can also be experimentally identified without state tomography, and further present a corresponding lower bound of genuine tripartite entanglement concurrence.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Fan Wang, Wen Zhou, Lin Chen, Shao-Ming Fei

item.title: A Compass on the Quantum State Sphere: The Hopf Ansatz for Arbitrary Pure-State Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.14231v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optimizing an arbitrary pure state requires more than a circuit that can prepare it: one also needs coordinates, local distance information, and measurable derivative directions. We introduce the Hopf ansatz, a binary-tree circuit for arbitrary normalized real and complex state vectors. Internal angles split probability between subtrees, while leaf phases supply the complex degrees of freedom. The same tree recovers physical angles from known amplitudes, gives an analytic diagonal metric on the state-vector sphere, and prepares each nonzero coordinate tangent as a normalized state. For Hamiltonian objectives and other costs with the same local transition-moment form, each gradient component is a known metric factor times a transition moment between the current state and a tangent state. Signed branch states express these moments through expectation-value measurements. Indexed preparation groups magnitude tangents by tree depth and collects complex phase tangents into one leaf-indexed block. The number of compiled gradient-access circuit families is logarithmic in Hilbert-space dimension; measurement repetitions needed for a prescribed accuracy remain a separate statistical cost. In deterministic real-state benchmarks with exact objectives and gradients and known global optima, metric-aware Hopf updates reach numerical-precision median gaps. Relative to coordinate-Adam baselines, they yield smaller mean final gaps in variational eigensolver tests and concentrate more runs at numerical precision in metrology-inspired tests. The Hopf ansatz thus supplies a compass for arbitrary pure-state optimization, with coordinates, geometry, and measurable directions in one circuit structure.
item.dc:creator: Ruge Lin, Guangxi Li

item.title: Geometric power capacity of coherent ergotropy in quantum batteries
item.description: arXiv:2607.16645v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore coherent ergotropy extraction in quantum batteries from a resource-geometric point of view. For an initial state $\rho$, we quantify the coherent extraction process by the coherent ergotropy $\mathcal{E}_c(\rho)$ and the coherent extraction distance $D_c^{\rm ext}(\rho)$ between the active state $\sigma_\rho$ and the passive state $P_\rho$. This defines the geometric power capacity $\Pi_c(\rho)=\mathcal{E}_c(\rho)/D_c^{\rm ext}(\rho)$, which measures the coherent ergotropy released unit minimal unitary distance. We prove that, for any driving Hamiltonian satisfying $\|V_t\|\leq\nu$, the actual coherent discharging power is bounded by $P_c^{\rm ext}(\rho;V_t)\leq \nu\Pi_c(\rho)$, showing that $\Pi_c(\rho)$ is a capacity under unit driving norm rather than the power of a particular protocol. General bounds on $\Pi_c(\rho)$ are derived by combining relative entropy bounds on coherent ergotropy with geometric bounds on the coherent extraction distance. We also formulate coherence measure induced bounds and protocol-corrected capacities involving the effective speed of a given Hamiltonian. Qubit and qutrit examples demonstrate that $\Pi_c(\rho)$ captures a resource-geometric feature of coherent discharging beyond coherent ergotropy or coherence measures alone.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Ping Xuan, Hua Nan, Zhi-Xi Wang, Shao-Ming Fei

item.title: Picosecond-resolved entanglement distribution over an urban free-space channel
item.description: arXiv:2607.21093v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-evolving entangled states describe quantum particles whose correlations evolve in time according to a well-defined dynamics. Such states can be generated in a variety of physical systems and are promising resources for several quantum technologies, ranging from quantum clock synchronization to quantum communication. However, their full potential is currently limited by the fact that the entanglement dynamics often occur on timescales comparable to the achievable synchronization precision, especially in experiments aimed at distributing entanglement through noisy urban channels. In this context, accurate timing is not merely a technical detail, but a fundamental requirement for faithfully observing and exploiting the underlying quantum correlations. Here, we demonstrate the faithful distribution of a fast-evolving entangled state over a 270 m free-space channel connecting two buildings in the center of Rome. The developed system incorporates a synchronization device capable of achieving sub-50 ps timing accuracy between the two ends of the link while simultaneously supporting channel stabilization. Our results demonstrate that time-evolving entanglement can be reliably transmitted through a noisy urban free-space channel, representing an important benchmark toward long-distance free-space quantum communication and the future implementation of time-correlated entangled states in demanding scenarios such as satellite-based quantum networks.
