item.title: QSCI-CMP: Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction with Chemically Motivated Preselection
item.description: arXiv:2608.05766v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present QSCI-CMP, a quantum-classical hybrid algorithm for molecular ground-state calculations that reduces both the query count and the gate count of sample-based quantum diagonalization with amplitude amplification (SQD-AA). SQD-AA mitigates the measurement bottleneck of quantum-selected configuration interaction (QSCI) by amplifying the basis states that have not yet been measured. Its oracle, however, specifies the measured states by listing them one by one, so its gate count grows with the number of collected states. Moreover, the quantum resources are spent even on states whose importance is evident from chemical knowledge, such as low-order excitations from the Hartree-Fock reference, which could be collected classically at the outset. We therefore propose to fix such chemically trivial states in advance, include them in the diagonalization subspace from the start, and exclude them from the amplification target, using a low-cost oracle that recognizes them through the excitation level and the seniority number of each basis state. We numerically demonstrate that QSCI-CMP reduces the query count and the gate count required to reach chemical accuracy by up to approximately 68% and 72% relative to SQD-AA for 24-qubit systems. The chemically trivial subspace is freely tunable within the classical computational budget. A larger subspace shifts more work onto the classical solver and increases the reduction in quantum cost, and when it captures the ground state sufficiently well, no quantum sampling is needed at all. We also point out that a query-optimal iteration count known from the analysis of quantum search further reduces the query count of both methods by approximately 12%.
item.dc:creator: Masahiko Kamoshita, Kosuke Mitarai

item.title: Spectral Localization in Cavity-Mediated Entanglement Harvesting
item.description: arXiv:2608.13449v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the relation between spectral localization and entanglement harvesting in an analytically solvable model of two qubits coupled to a leaky single-mode cavity, which in turn couples to a continuous electromagnetic bath. We derive the no-jump concurrence at a prescribed reference gate time in closed form, $\mathcal C_g(Q)=2e^{-\pi/(2Q)}(1+e^{-\pi/(2Q)})/(1+3e^{-\pi/Q})$, where $Q\equiv|\Delta|/\kappa$ is the ratio of the qubit-cavity detuning $\Delta$ to the cavity linewidth $\kappa$. This reference time is inherited from the first maximally entangling unitary gate. At finite loss, $\mathcal C_g$ is the conditional concurrence at this prescribed readout time. In the high-$Q$ limit, $\mathcal C_g\simeq1-\pi^2/(16Q^2)$, while in the low-$Q$ limit it decays exponentially. For the Lorentzian spectral family, $Q$ is proportional to a detuning-normalized inverse participation ratio and simultaneously measures the balance between coherent exchange and collective decay. This yields a compact, model-specific description of the crossover from nearly unit conditional entanglement to overdamped suppression. The predicted $\mathcal C_g(Q)$ curve can, in principle, be examined in circuit QED with ideal monitoring and no-jump post-selection.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: The exact price of local realism in CHSH experiments: a measurement-dependence-detection trade-off surface, a moir\'e phase-locking mechanism that saturates it, and an unmeasured fringe in the fourfold coincidence sum
item.description: arXiv:2608.18886v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For local hidden-variable accounts of the CHSH experiment that are faithful -- reproducing the observed singles and coincidence rates and unbiased marginals of a polarization singlet with symmetric detector efficiency $\eta_{\rm eff}$ -- I determine the minimal measurement dependence $M$ (Hall's measure) needed to reach a CHSH value $S$. Linear programming over all local strategies yields, to machine precision, $M(S,\eta_{\rm eff})=\max\{0,\eta_{\rm eff}((S+2)\eta_{\rm eff}-4)/6\}$, whose edges reproduce Hall's bound, the Garg-Mermin threshold, and the postselection ceiling. The quantum point is certified exactly: $M(2\sqrt{2},9/10)=(27\sqrt{2}-33)/100$, by primal and dual certificates in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$. I solve the unique detection profile under which a deterministic sign model reproduces the singlet exactly, and prove exact quantum correlations and angle-independent coincidence rates jointly impossible in this class. Mixtures of this profile with measurement dependence trade $M$ against a $\cos 4(a-b)$ modulation of the fourfold coincidence sum, up to 12.4% in relative amplitude, taking identical values at the two CHSH relative angles; existing data exclude its full amplitude and bound its mixtures with flat detection to a detection share of order 15%; its sub-percent content is unbounded. A two-setting cross-ratio and a settings-torus log-Fourier protocol, both calibrated against channel-efficiency imbalance, reach $5\sigma$ at 0.1% within hours: a flat result excludes the solved family to a detection share of order 1%; a surviving fringe would be a joint $(a,b)$ dependence no single-pair apparatus produces. I exhibit a local mechanism, moir\'e phase locking, with deterministic phase evolution and randomness in a quenched ensemble, which attains the certified floor exactly at $\eta_{\rm eff}=1$ and, with the solved profile, reaches $M=0$ at $\eta_{\rm eff}\approx 0.80$.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Alai

item.title: Quantifying Nonstabilizerness of Codeword-Stabilized Codes
item.description: arXiv:2608.22017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universal quantum computation requires non-Clifford gates, which stabilizer codes can provide transversally only up to a finite level of the Clifford hierarchy. Non-stabilizer codes are not subject to this bound and are the natural candidates to fill the gap. However, it is difficult to efficiently evaluate the nonstabilizerness (or magic) of non-stabilizer codes. Here, we resolve this problem for codeword-stabilized (CWS) codes by showing that the nonstabilizerness of a CWS code is determined by the difference structure of its codewords. Whenever a Sidon set of the required size exists, the most magical codes are related to the Sidon sets, whose pairwise differences are all distinct. Structural analysis demonstrates that nonstabilizerness is invariant under coset closure, giving rise to non-stabilizer codes with arbitrarily many logical qubits and constant nonstabilizerness. Nonstabilizerness of whole code families becomes exactly computable, and we obtain closed-form values for the Kerdock codes. Moreover, we reveal a tradeoff between nonstabilizerness and transversal gates. For a code with $k$ logical qubits, a diagonal transversal gate that is non-Clifford on $t$ coordinates forces the nonstabilizerness benchmark to be at most $2(k-t)$. These results reduce the search for codes with high nonstabilizerness and for transversal non-Clifford gates to classical counting problems, to which the standard tools of additive combinatorics apply.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liu, Ke-Mi Xu

item.title: Exact quantum splitting and the structure of finite algebras
item.description: arXiv:2608.30340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For squarefree $f\in\F_q[x]$, Berlekamp's fixed-point algebra is $B\cong\F_q^r$, where $r$ is the number of irreducible factors. We give an exact quantum splitting procedure in a circuit model permitting efficiently computable, input-dependent single-qubit rotations. For a block with $s\ge2$ factors, a quadratic-character test (odd $q$) or absolute-trace test (characteristic $2$) is nonconstant with an exactly known probability $p_{q,s}\ge1/2$. Its value depends only on $q,s$, not on the hidden factors. An auxiliary-qubit reduction to success probability $1/4$ makes one Grover iteration exact. Thus factorization takes exactly $r-1$ splitting rounds and $O(n^3\log q)$ quantum $\F_q$-operations, with deterministic polynomial classical preprocessing and bookkeeping. The method also extracts primitive idempotents of arbitrary finite-dimensional commutative unital algebras given by structure constants in $O(n^4\log q)$ quantum $\F_q$-operations, staying over $\F_q$ throughout. Computing the radical and passing to the center extends it to the decomposition of $A/\Rad(A)$ into simple two-sided ideals, for an arbitrary finite-dimensional associative $\F_q$-algebra $A$.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Imran

item.title: Predictive Structure Behind Rare Outcomes in Random Quantum Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2609.17482v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Local random quantum circuits selected for unusually large output peaks reveal intermediate-state structure that predicts new peak formation and guides circuit construction. In one-dimensional Haar-random brickwall circuits, the selected trajectories combine stronger pairwise correlations and probability redistribution with lower bipartite entanglement and output entropy. We test the predictive value of this structure by keeping each circuit's initial segment fixed and independently regenerating the remaining gates. Across the tested size-depth grid at n=8-14, peak-selected states have higher new-peak probability than normal/nonpeak controls, with an overall probability ratio of 3.23 at the primary depths. Within a separate unconditioned ensemble, a fixed structural score computed from the initial segment predicts new-peak probability and gives a 1.86-fold yield gain in a replay with equal numbers of remaining-circuit evaluations. Randomizing relative phases while preserving computational-basis probabilities strongly attenuates the selected-state advantage, demonstrating a functional contribution from relative-phase organization. Structural and phase-intervention tests extend to n=16. Structure-guided gate selection improves high-peak yield under common local refinement, while guidance using multiple intermediate observables improves new-peak probability over peak-only guidance in all 16 tested size-depth settings. Together, these results show how intermediate-state structure can predict and promote new peak formation under finite-depth local dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Myeongsu Kim, Travis Humble, Sabre Kais

item.title: clifford_qc: A Python Toolkit for Quantum Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2609.23059v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: clifford_qc is a Python research toolkit for constructing quantum models, comparing variational and subspace eigensolvers, and estimating measurement resources. A common sparse Pauli algebra connects Hamiltonians, density operators, gates, and candidate-selection observables; dedicated interfaces handle circuits, execution, and statistical estimates. A worked gradient example illustrates shared measurements, and a molecular workflow separates reusable preparation, solving, and reference validation. Matrix-element banks support virtual subspaces, exact Ritz residuals, and folded-spectrum roots. Process-isolated benchmarks show that packed coefficients and streaming reduce observed peak memory on the larger tested inputs at increased runtime. Measurement studies separate setting counts, shot requirements, and device cost: fully commuting readout certifies a fixed first-order Ritz functional with fewer shots, while anticommuting cliques help some fixed reference energies and not others. Entangling-gate time and connectivity can offset shot savings or make a protocol inadmissible under illustrative device models. Further studies expose subspace bias, indeterminate encoding comparisons, failed approximate-restriction screens, and high residual-measurement costs under the tested uniform allocations. Generated tables, provenance records, a versioned evidence contract, and manuscript checks connect claims to their inputs. These small-system results support reproducible method development and establish neither hardware performance nor a general simulation speedup.
item.dc:creator: Ginanjar Utama, Hermawan Kresno Dipojono

item.title: A sharp norm inequality for entanglement-breaking channels
item.description: arXiv:2609.27906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a channel $\Phi$ on $M_d$ written in the generalised Bloch parameterisation $r \mapsto Ar+c$, we prove that entanglement breaking implies $\|A\|_*^2 + \frac{d(d-1)}{2}\,|c|^2 \;\le\; (d-1)^2 ,$ where $\|\cdot\|_*$ denotes the nuclear norm. Read on the Choi state of the channel, the inequality is an instance of the covariance-matrix criterion of Gittsovich et al.; what is added here is an elementary proof in Holevo form and a complete description of the equality cases. Apart from the constant channel onto a pure state, which shows that the coefficient $d(d-1)/2$ cannot be increased, equality holds exactly for the measure-and-prepare channels with rank-one effects $\alpha_k|e_k\rangle\langle e_k|$ and pure outputs $|\psi_k\rangle\langle\psi_k|$ whose overlaps are an affine image of those of the measurement directions, $|\langle\psi_j|\psi_k\rangle|^2 = P + (1-P)\,(d|\langle e_j|e_k\rangle|^2 - 1)/(d-1)$ for a common $P = \mathrm{Tr}\,\Phi(\mathbf{1}/d)^2$. These include the completely dephasing channel, the re-preparation channel of every rank-one POVM, a one-parameter family interpolating between dephasing and the constant channel, and non-unital non-projective examples already at $d = 2$. The qubit case reads $\|A\|_*^2+|c|^2\le1$ and extends to full rank a rank-two condition of Ruskai. The proof sharpens Ruskai's bound $\|A\|_*\le1$ by retaining the POVM completeness relation $\sum_k f_k=0$, which her argument discards; this recentres $A$ from a second moment into a cross-covariance, and is the entire content of the improvement.
item.dc:creator: Eran Kopel

item.title: Broadband and Large-Multimode Quantum Optical Storage with Rare-Earth Ions in Solids
item.description: arXiv:2609.28271v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Broadband quantum memory devices are essential elements for future quantum networks. Here we propose a broadband quantum memory scheme called Hole Anti-hole Grating Echo Memory (HAGEM) for rare-earth ions in solids, which can be implemented with most of the present rare-earth ions hosted in various types of solids. Using HAGEM, a quantum memory device with one billion temporal modes per second can be developed with current available technologies. To validate the memory protocol, we conducted some proof-of-concept experiments. We provide a Eu$^\text{{3+}}$ molecular complex with special hyperfine level structures of which the hyperfine level separations are in a specific mathematical correlation that can be obtained by harnessing chemical engineering. Using the proposed memory protocol and material, we experimentally demonstrate a single-mode quantum optical storage efficiency of 14.9% and a memory bandwidth of 200MHz, which can easily be extended to a few GHz. In addition, a multi-mode storage of four temporal modes is achieved with a storage efficiency of 1.3%. Broadband & large-multimode quantum memory device with a long storage time enabled by HAGEM integrating with the current available entangled photon pair source and tunable delay lines, a quantum repeater network with an entanglement distribution rate on the order of 1kHz - 10kHz can be created with a communication distance around 100km. This will greatly facilitate the development of quantum networks in near future.
item.dc:creator: Yisheng Lei, Senthil Kumar Kuppusamy, Idris Tlemsani, Suma Al-Hunaishi, Pengrui Jiao, Olaf Fuhr, Mario Ruben, Philippe Goldner, Diana Serrano

item.title: Universal holonomic control of algebras of observables
item.description: arXiv:2609.28662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend geometric parallel transport from states and degenerate eigenspaces to observable algebras defining generalized quantum subsystems. At fixed block structure, unitary invariance fixes a unique connection, recovering Berry--Wilczek--Zee transport on bands. On positive-dimensional strata, its holonomy is the special-unitary part of the normalizer: all inner logical gates and equal-type sector permutations are attainable. Given a compatible gapped Hamiltonian and access to the required paths, inner gates can be implemented adiabatically by isospectral control of a band refinement.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Zanardi

item.title: Qaiji IR: An Eight-Layer Intermediate Representation Family for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Compilation
item.description: arXiv:2609.29305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical compilation relates ideal operations and measurement outcomes to control pulses and device instructions. Existing formats each describe part of this process, and their preservation checks are often specific to one tool rather than to a common intermediate representation (IR). I present Qaiji-IR, an eight-layer IR family organized by a five-axis semantic contract for data, semantics, lowering, runtime, and verification. Its implementation provides typed circuits, an operation-semantics layer (L4) that records operation structure and checks a bounded set of equivalence rules, and a native-scheduling layer (L2) with separate validation. Nine circuit pairs are compared with ideal reference calculations. An aggregate baseline, which compares operation categories and measurement counts, accepts four behavior-changing transformations: gate reordering and changes of rotation angle, operand, or measurement destination. The L4 checker passes none of them. It distinguishes strict equality from equality up to global phase and returns unsupported when its rules cannot decide, as for valid rotation fusion. L2 validation checks native schedules against their source circuits, decomposition rules, local matrices, and configured timing. A single-qubit active-reset program is compiled through the Qaiji-IR frontend, a syntax adapter, and the EmuPlat backend into pulses and device instructions for a virtual pulse processing unit (VPPU). Injected binary outcomes select the conditional drive. Backend predicate tests reveal incorrect execution for equality to zero and for a nonbinary feedback value. This backend path does not use the validated L2 schedule. Physical measurement feedback, calibrated pulse fidelity, and feedback latency require further work.
item.dc:creator: Jun Ye

item.title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
item.description: arXiv:2609.30159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-Abelian quantum codes connect quantum error correction, phases of matter, and computational resources. In this work, we develop a general framework for constructing non-Abelian quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes by gauging sheaf codes via cup products and use it to establish code families with constant encoding rate and linear distance, simultaneously achieving optimal asymptotic scaling in both parameters. In particular, we characterize explicit logical representatives of the full gauged code space, and provide a fundamental treatment of non-Abelian code distance in the sense of Knill--Laflamme based on combining expansion with cleaning to establish protection against arbitrary errors. We further construct an almost-good family with entire code spaces exhibiting long-range magic. Moreover, we use linearly addressable cup product to directly generate linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements of Clifford operators. These results extend good qLDPC codes beyond the Pauli stabilizer setting, lay the foundation for pursuing the no low-energy trivial magic conjecture and shed light on non-Abelian quantum phases and orders beyond geometric locality.
item.dc:creator: Zimu Li, Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu

item.title: Quantum algorithms for the exponentiation of Toeplitz matrices and applications in partial differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2609.31372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present quantum algorithms to approximate the exponential of banded Toeplitz matrices. These matrices have central importance in many PDE related problems, but their quantum implementation is hindered by their possibly large norms. Constructing directly the exponential we can circumvent this limitation. By relating the lower/upper shift operators to circulant and skewcirculant generators, which are diagonalised by the QFT, we construct (i) an LCU-based block encoding of banded Toeplitz matrices, (ii) an efficient, controllably truncated Pauli-string decomposition of the circulant eigenphases with a closed-form error bound, and (iii) a specialized QFT-Trotter product formula. As an application we build a block encoding of the propagator of the discretised heat equation with periodic, Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, using a frequency cutoff.
item.dc:creator: Xabier Guti\'errez, Nicola Mariella, Javier Gonz\'alez-Conde, Sergiy Zhuk, Mikel Sanz

item.title: Quantum--classical break-even in electronic dynamics of macrocyclic molecules
item.description: arXiv:2609.39693v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Here we demonstrate quantum--classical break-even for chemical dynamics applications, reaching useful accuracy with a quantum-hardware wall-clock time comparable to that estimated for practical classical computing resources. To this end, we develop a workflow for problems that are hardware-native but classically hard. We target large ring-shaped molecules that map naturally onto quantum hardware with neighboring connections. Exploiting the spatial locality of interactions, we compress short-time evolution within a small region using tensor networks. We then use rotational symmetry to replicate the compressed circuit in space and time, enabling long-time dynamics of large systems with practical classical processing times. We apply the workflow to conjugated macrocycles with rotational periodicity, 12-qubit benzene and 120-qubit [60]annulene, by embedding their electronic structure onto loops of IBM quantum processors. For the annulene, we compared the quantum-processing-unit (QPU) wall-clock times for hole-doped nonequilibrium dynamics to the estimated wall-clock time of two state-of-the-art classical methods, Majorana propagation and matrix-product-state time evolution based on the time-dependent variational principle. We show a situation in which a hybrid quantum--classical strategy is comparable to a classical-only counterpart in terms of both accuracy and computational time for a conventional high-performance computing system under ideal parallelization. These results show that quantum hardware can become a realistic computational option for chemical simulations for practitioners in chemical science and engineering.
item.dc:creator: Shu Kanno, Kenji Sugisaki, Takashi Imamichi, Toshinari Itoko, Rei Sakuma, Hajime Nakamura, Qi Gao, Naoki Yamamoto

item.title: Real-Time Adaptive Filtering and the Boxcar Limit in Superconducting Qubit Readout
item.description: arXiv:2610.00783v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Control and readout systems for superconducting quantum computing support real-time control and high-fidelity qubit-state discrimination. We examine when additional digital processing improves readout fidelity. A common baseline for dispersive readout uses a boxcar averager to compute a uniformly weighted average over a fixed window followed by threshold-based state assignment. We evaluated an adaptive finite-impulse-response (FIR) filter trained in real time using the least-mean-squares (LMS) algorithm on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) quantum controller. We also analyzed measured readout shots offline to compare the frozen filter with boxcar averaging, and evaluate per-sample weighting plus sequential detection. For the fixed FIR filters tested, summing the filtered samples gives the boxcar sum multiplied by one complex number apart from a small edge correction. We call this the kernel collapse. The multiplication scales the state separation and noise equally without improving state discrimination, and we call this the boxcar limit. The frozen LMS filter reduces trace noise, but shows no resolved improvement in readout fidelity. On a 2D transmon, optimizing the readout window accounted for much of the improvement over full-window integration. We then examined how changing the decision method could reduce calibration effort and decision time. On a higher-fidelity 3D ancilla readout, our modeled template estimation reached the same fidelity target as direct averaging with 89.8% fewer labeled shots per state. Offline sequential replay assigned most shots before the acquisition window ended. These results distinguish waveform denoising from state-discrimination improvement, and motivate direct control of decision weights and assignment time in dispersive readout.
item.dc:creator: Hans Johnson, Tanay Roy, Leonardo Bove, David van Zanten, Silvia Zorzetti, Jafar Saniie

item.title: Nonlinear quantum multi-spin dynamics without entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.05521v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a distinct route for extending classical atomistic spin dynamics into the quantum regime for arbitrary spin $s$, based on a variational product-state \textit{ansatz} that includes both pure and mixed local states. By construction, intersite entanglement -- expected to remain negligible even on very short time scales in many real materials -- is excluded, while local quantum effects are retained through the nonclassical structure of $s\geq 1$ density operators. Nonlinear dynamics arise from both the mean-field interdependence of the local states and the state-dependent dissipative terms. The framework recovers classical spin dynamics for $s=\frac{1}{2}$ while allowing genuinely quantum local dynamics for higher spins. It clarifies the variational and geometric origin of the inequivalence between quantum Landau-Lifshitz and Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics, provides a criterion for their equivalence under a common time rescaling, establishes connections with the classical theory through two qualitatively distinct limits ($s\to\infty$ and a large number of quantum spins $N$), and allows realistic $\mathcal{O}(N)$ simulations of quantum spin dynamics in materials.
item.dc:creator: Ivan P. Miranda, Erik Sj\"oqvist

item.title: Characterizing Fermionic Non-Gaussianity in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model via Replica Twist Entropy
item.description: arXiv:2610.10123v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of quantum many-body systems plays a central role in modern many-body physics. Intriguing insights emerge from investigating how quantum resources, which are essential for achieving unambiguous quantumness, are generated and spread under chaotic quantum dynamics. In fermionic systems, non-Gaussianity constitutes an important resource beyond entanglement, characterizing the deviation of generic quantum states from free-fermion states. In this Letter, we propose using the \textit{replica twist entropy}, defined through the expectation value of a replica rotation operator with a tunable angle $\alpha$, as a natural probe of non-Gaussianity in pure fermionic states. After deriving its behavior for typical many-body states, we establish a general framework for analyzing the replica twist entropy in solvable Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev models in the large-$N$ limit. Applying this framework to the dynamics of the thermofield double state, we uncover a novel dynamical phase diagram in the parameter space of $\alpha$ and evolution time $t$, exhibiting spontaneous $Z_2$ symmetry breaking at $\alpha=\pi/4$ and universal cusps as a function of $\alpha$ in the long-time regime. Our results pave the way for studying non-Gaussianity in strongly correlated fermionic systems and reveal a new class of dynamical transitions probed by non-Gaussianity.
item.dc:creator: Ning Sun, Pengfei Zhang

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.12908v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the second of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on Shelah's independence property. An observable without it has idealized responses of the first Baire class, and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy for Rosenthal compacta divides such observables into three classes, each containing a physical order. In the transverse-field Ising model, the spontaneous magnetization decides whether the family of magnetizations is stable or lies in the second class.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

item.title: Riemannian Formulation of Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Solvers for Elliptic Problems: Energy-Norm Guarantees and Duct-Flow Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.15586v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sample-based quantum linear solvers measure quantum Krylov states $e^{-iAT}|b\rangle$ and reconstruct the solution of $Ax=b$ classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for positive-definite systems that arise from elliptic partial differential equations. We show that the sampling guarantees hold in any fixed basis with an efficient transform. We then replace the variational reconstruction by a Galerkin solve on the sampled set. For this reconstruction we derive expected and high-probability energy-norm error bounds, a sample complexity in terms of the smallest sampling probability on an essential set, a computable residual certificate, and a support-completeness theorem for the dephased outcome law. We formulate the method for elliptic problems on Riemannian cross sections. In two dimensions the stiffness matrix is metric-independent in conformal coordinates, and curved vessels lead to the same matrix class. Killing symmetries of the cross section give selection rules for the measurement outcomes, and the Lie derivative of the metric gives first-order bounds for geometric perturbations. We separate operator approximations, whose effect we bound, from sampler approximations, which affect coverage but not the target. As examples we treat the implicit step of pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts. In simulations of up to 12 qubits, the number of Fourier modes required for 1% error grows from 14 to 60 while the number of unknowns grows from 64 to 4096. A classical residual-greedy selection is nevertheless more efficient than quantum sampling in all cases studied, consistent with the low measured sampling efficiency. On a six-qubit trapped-ion processor, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model whose strength grows by about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity selection rule rejects shots at the predicted rate.
item.dc:creator: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Villa Park, California, USA), Byeongyong Park (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

item.title: Scalable Tomography of Coherent Noise via Stabilizer-Code Polarization
item.description: arXiv:2610.19779v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent errors accumulate linearly rather than diffusively, making them invisible to Pauli-twirl-based char- acterization. It poses a central challenge for quantum error correction, yet its characterization typically requires multi-qubit process tomography whose cost grows exponentially with system size. We show that measurement- free error correction projects arbitrary few-qubit coherent noise onto a fixed single-logical-qubit effective chan- nel, enabling tomography at constant cost. Exploiting the polarization effects of bit-flip and phase-flip codes, we construct a concatenated effective-channel fingerprint and prove, by a parity-based contradiction argument, that the observation map is globally injective over a prescribed coherent-noise family; hence the underlying noise parameters are uniquely recovered without any sparsity or low-rank assumptions. The recovered coherent noise model can be fed into decoding algorithms; relative to independent noise priors, we expect this to reduce the logical error rate for surface-code decoders. The protocol offers a scalable route to coherent-noise identification whenever the noise admits a moderate-dimensional parameterization.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang

item.title: Hankel Submatrices with Bounded Word Length: Dimension Tradeoffs in Probabilistic and Quantum Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.21797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the largest admissible side length of fixed-margin square Hankel submatrices generated by probabilistic realizations on a \(d\)-point carrier and quantum linear realizations on a \(d\)-dimensional Hilbert space, when prefix and suffix word lengths are bounded by \(T\). Using a four-symbol transition alphabet shared by all selected rows and columns, we show that, for fixed margins \(\lambda_2>0\) and \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2<1\), the corresponding side lengths satisfy \(\ln N_{\mathsf Q,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d^2,T\})\) for completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) quantum realizations and \(\ln N_{\mathsf S,4}=\Theta_{\lambda_1,\lambda_2}(\min\{d,T\})\) for probabilistic automata. Four unitary and four permutation transition maps attain the corresponding orders. At zero false-acceptance tolerance (\(\lambda_2=0\) with \(0\leq\lambda_1<1\)), all four model classes satisfy \(\ln N=\Theta(\min\{\ln d,T\})\). The upper bounds follow from state-space packing and word counting, while the lower bounds combine explicit transition tuples with Grassmannian and positive-rate codebooks whose existence follows from the probabilistic method. These results establish sharp dimension--word-length tradeoffs for bounded-word Hankel tables.
item.dc:creator: Yixin Zhao

item.title: Gyrators for superconducting circuit design
item.description: arXiv:2610.22145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assuming only the solubility of Kirchhoff's laws, the conservation of energy, and the form of the constitutive relations, we present a flux-charge symmetric Hamiltonian formalism that always admits a symplectic reduction for nonsingular, well-posed circuits involving gyrators, inductors, and capacitors (LCG circuits) with arbitrary non-linearity. The formalism introduces a notion of circuit duality on non-linear non-reciprocal circuits and a family of point transformations that inserts, removes, and moves reciprocal elements across gyrators while preserving the Hamiltonian spectrum. With these transformations, we extend Tellegen's classic result that gyrators make reciprocal elements behave as their dual to non-linear reciprocal elements such as the Josephson junction and quantum phase slip. Furthermore, we present conditions under which non-reciprocal circuits can be transformed to dynamically equivalent reciprocal circuits.
item.dc:creator: Ciro Salcedo, Sasha Cocquyt, Andrew A. Houck, Andrew Osborne

item.title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
item.description: arXiv:2610.23507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bayesian inference enables self-consistent plasma parameter inversion in tokamak integrated data analysis by fusing multi-source diagnostics. However, under nonlinear Gaussian likelihoods, finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimate typically relies on sampling methods whose high computational overhead precludes real-time plasma control. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Bayesian inversion framework using a Coherent Ising Machine (CIM)-a quantum computing architecture based on coupled degenerate optical parametric oscillators (DOPOs). With native all-to-all connectivity, the CIM directly maps the negative log-posterior potential onto a spin Hamiltonian and leverages quantum vacuum fluctuations for rapid state-space search during pitchfork bifurcation. Validated on plasma current profile inversion for the EAST tokamak, this method achieves a single-run solution time of approximately 1 ms. Although current qubit limits necessitate a block-wise iterative scheme that prevents full real-time execution today, rapidly scaling quantum hardware offers a clear pathway toward real-time tokamak control.
item.dc:creator: Zijie Liu, Wenchao Liu, Yao Huang, Kai Wen, Yuehang Wang, Wenxin Li, Zhengping Luo, Anzhe Jiang, Wangyi Rui, Hongdong Zhu, Kai Wu, Qi Gao, Bihao Guo, Jingjing Wang, Shuai Li, Yin Ma, Dalong Chen, Hai Wei, Qiping Yuan, Bingjia Xiao, Jiangang Li

item.title: On the geometry of quantum constrained systems
item.description: arXiv:0801.1119v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometric methods have proved useful in the Hamiltonian description of classical constrained systems. We develop the corresponding geometry for quantum constrained systems, using the formulation of quantum mechanics in which the space of rays $\Ps$ is a K\"ahler manifold and unitary transformations are its canonical transformations. The Dirac conditions $\hat C_i\Psi=0$ define the zero set of a single function $\Cq=\ev{\Mop}$, the expectation value of the master constraint operator. Our central identity is $\Cq=|\mu|^2+\tfrac12\|X_\mu\|^2$, where $\mu=(\ev{\hat C_i})$ is the moment map of the gauge action on $\Ps$ and $X_\mu$ its fundamental vector fields: the quantum condition imposes the classical-type condition $\mu=0$ \emph{and} the collapse of the gauge orbits to points. This explains why no second reduction is needed. The physical state space is a totally geodesic K\"ahler submanifold. $\Cq$ is a Morse--Bott function which gradient flow is heat-kernel-smeared group averaging, converges to the nearest-point projection onto physical states, and its fibres are invariant under the complexified gauge group. Physical observables are characterised to all orders by the double-commutator condition, which is equivalent to $[\hat O,\hat P_0]=0$, with $\hat P_0$ the projector onto physical states. When zero lies in the continuous spectrum, the gradient flow converges to Dirac states in the sense of Grundling and Hurst, and its large-time asymptotics reproduce the rigging map of refined algebraic quantization. Finally, pulled back along coherent states, $\Cq$ equals the classical master constraint plus an $O(\hbar)$ term given by the squared speed of the classical gauge orbits. Together these results connect the Dirac procedure, the master constraint programme, refined algebraic quantization and symplectic reduction within one geometric picture.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Corichi

item.title: Dynamical Coherence Measures
item.description: arXiv:2401.07127v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present three measures of the dynamical coherence of channels, which generalize several previous results. The measures are based on a generalized distance-like function between channels, such as a quantum divergence of channels, including the relative entropy and diamond distance. Free operations are considered to be detection-incoherent, creation-incoherent, and detection-creation incoherent. We consider free superchannels constructed from free pre- and post-processing channels. The new measures are monotone under free superchannels and convex.
item.dc:creator: Anna Vershynina

item.title: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2405.06720v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One-photon annihilation of the bound electron-positron pair in the field of atomic nuclei is investigated. In our analysis the central atomic nucleus is assumed to be an infinitely heavy, positively charged and point `particle' with the electric charge $Q e$. The explicit formulas for the both annihilation cross section and one-photon annihilation rate $\Gamma^{(b)}_{1 \gamma}$ are derived and discussed. We also derive and discuss the closed formula which describes the angular distribution of the emitted photons. All our formulas can directly be used to evaluate probabilities of the actual one-photon annihilation in various atoms, ions and light molecular ions which also contain one (or two) positron(s).
item.dc:creator: Alexei M. Frolov

item.title: Nanoparticle arrays levitated in a cavity for quantum sensing
item.description: arXiv:2406.00366v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Levitated nanoparticles are being investigated as ultrasensitive quantum sensors of forces and accelerations, with applications ranging from fundamental physics phenomena such as dark matter or quantum gravity to real world applications. Attention is now turning to multiparticle regimes, and an important question is whether collective effects offer advantages for sensing. We investigate here the spectral characteristics of collective motion of $N $ trapped nanoparticles interacting via the optical mode of a cavity. We find the collective motion typically exhibit two generic spectral features: a broad spectral feature, the collective bright mode (CBM) which has been previously studied; but we find also a new structure of sharp peaks , the mechanical mode comb (MMC). We can describe all the detailed spectral features of the system, with a simple closed-form expression, by reducing the motion to a 1D generic collective mode which is non-Hermitian. We show that the MMC is more advantageous than the usual CBM for increased sensitivity in force sensing. We find that the mechanical comb can autonomously repair loss of `teeth' due to particle loss, a feature that may offer robustness in sensing.
item.dc:creator: J. H. Iacoponi, M. Rademacher, T. S. Monteiro

item.title: Absorbing state transitions with long-range annihilation
item.description: arXiv:2409.03280v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a family of classical stochastic processes describing diffusive particles undergoing branching and long-range annihilation in the presence of a parity constraint. The probability for a pair-annihilation event decays as a power-law in the distance between particles, with a tunable exponent. Such long-range processes arise naturally in various classical settings, and increasingly play a role in the study of quantum dynamics: for example, quantum state preparation or error correction processes aim to prepare ordered ground states, which requires removing point-like excitations in pairs via non-local feedback operations conditioned on a global set of measurement outcomes. We analytically and numerically describe features of absorbing phases and phase transitions in this family of classical models as pairwise annihilation is performed at larger and larger distances. Notably, we find that the two canonical absorbing-state universality classes -- directed-percolation and parity-conserving -- are endpoints of a new line of universality classes with continuously varying critical exponents. These new classes follow from an interplay of long-range interactions and symmetries: decreasing the long-range exponent effectively weakens the local effects of global symmetry constraints. This competition significantly broadens known non-equilibrium phases and phase transitions.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas O'Dea, Sayak Bhattacharjee, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Vedika Khemani

item.title: Nonlinear Landau levels in the almost-bosonic anyon gas
item.description: arXiv:2510.14679v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an average-field description becomes appropriate for the low-energy collective state of the gas. Namely, by means of a Hartree-Jastrow ansatz, we derive a two-parameter Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger energy functional which extends the well-known Gross-Pitaevskii / nonlinear Schr\"odinger density functional theory to the magnetic (anyonic) self-interaction. One parameter determines the total number of self-generated magnetic flux units in the system, and the other the effective strength of spin-orbit self-interaction. This latter interaction can be either attractive/focusing or repulsive/defocusing, and depends both on the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction and the relative length scale of the flux profile of the anyons. Densities and energies of ground and excited states are studied analytically and numerically for a wide range of the parameters and align well with a sequence of exact nonlinear Landau levels describing Jackiw-Pi self-dual solitons. With increasing flux, counter-rotating vortices are formed, enhancing the stability of the gas against collapse. Apart from clarifying the relations between various different anyon models that have appeared in the literature, our analysis sheds new light on the many-anyon spectral problem, and also exemplifies a novel supersymmetry-breaking phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Ataei, Ask Ellingsen, Filippa Getzner, Th\'eotime Girardot, Douglas Lundholm, Dinh-Thi Nguyen

item.title: Combinatorial properties of holographic entropy inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2601.09987v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A holographic entropy inequality (HEI) is a linear inequality obeyed by Ryu-Takayanagi holographic entanglement entropies, or equivalently by the minimum cut function on weighted graphs. We establish a new combinatorial framework for studying HEIs, and use it to prove several properties they share, including two majorization-related properties as well as a necessary and sufficient condition for an inequality to be an HEI. We thereby resolve all the conjectures presented in [arXiv:2508.21823], proving two of them and disproving the other two. In particular, we show that the null reduction of any superbalanced HEI passes the majorization test defined in [arXiv:2508.21823], thereby providing strong new evidence that all HEIs are obeyed in time-dependent holographic states.
item.dc:creator: Guglielmo Grimaldi, Matthew Headrick, Veronika E. Hubeny, Pavel Shteyner

item.title: Time-Dependent Wave-Packet Approach to Reactions for Quantum Computation
item.description: arXiv:2603.26881v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a method for obtaining the scattering matrix for nuclear or chemical reactions on a finite lattice. Aside from the preparation of the initial and final states as wave packets, the only other operation required is unitary time evolution, making this approach ideal for simulations on quantum hardware. The central quantity is a time-dependent overlap between incoming and outgoing wave packets whose Fourier transform corresponds to the scattering matrix at fixed energy, from which one can calculate elastic and inelastic cross sections for reactions involving two interacting clusters. Working in Cartesian coordinates enables an efficient encoding of the problem on quantum hardware via the first quantization mapping, with favorable qubit scaling for describing asymptotic scattering states. Within this framework, we describe a quantum algorithm for probing the scattering amplitude through different angles, including the forward direction, which provides access to the total cross section via the optical theorem. We demonstrate our methods through a series of numerical examples, for both elastic and inelastic processes, comparing against exact calculations. The techniques we describe can more readily be extended to a large number of constituent particles than other existing approaches, once fault-tolerant quantum hardware becomes available.
item.dc:creator: Evan Rule, Ionel Stetcu

item.title: Boundary R\'enyi oscillations in the open XX chain
item.description: arXiv:2604.05356v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For the ground state of the semi-infinite XX chain with Fermi momentum $k_F$, we derive the extracted $2k_F$ contribution to the R\'enyi entropy of its first $\ell$ sites at fixed $\alpha>1$. Its phase $\sin[(2\ell+1)k_F]$ matches the Friedel oscillation at the entangling bond and becomes the even--odd alternation at half filling. An exact Hankel determinant reduction and Riemann--Hilbert analysis give every term $\mathcal{L}^{-(2q-1)/\alpha}$ for positive integers $q$ with $2q-1<\alpha$, where $\mathcal{L}=4\ell\sin k_F$, with an $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1})$ error within this extracted component for $k_F$ away from $0$ and $\pi$. At integer $\alpha=p\ge2$, exact factorization gives a finite sum over all roots with error $O(\mathcal{L}^{-1-1/p})$. We also determine the $2k_F$ terms of $\log Z_\alpha(\phi)$, where $Z_\alpha(\phi)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_A^\alpha e^{i\phi Q_A})$, $\rho_A$ is the block's reduced density matrix, and $Q_A$ is its fermion number. At fixed nonzero flux $|\phi|<\pi$ with $2q-1\mp\phi/\pi\ne\alpha$, the two exponential terms have different decay powers. Exact factorization sharpens the integer result. These pointwise estimates do not justify projection to fixed charge. The uncharged sequence and the two leading charged terms agree with earlier generalized Fisher--Hartwig predictions. Numerical calculations at $p=4$ test the predicted subleading coefficients without an adjustable normalization.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: Quantum matter is weakly entangled at low energies
item.description: arXiv:2604.14143v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct upper bounds on entanglement entropies of many-body quantum states that have fixed energy expectation values with respect to local Hamiltonians. Our focus is on entanglement entropies of subsystems that make up approximately half of the full system. The upper bound on the von Neumann entanglement entropy is half the sum of the thermal entropies of two fictitious systems at the same temperature as one another, with an additional area-law contribution in some systems. The effective temperature is chosen such that the sum of the thermal energies of the two fictitious systems matches the constraint on the energy of the state in the original problem; at subextensive energies, this temperature decreases with increasing system size. Our upper bounds on R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies take an analogous form. These inequalities show that, in systems that are frustration-free (FF) and whose zero-temperature subsystem thermal entropies scale with surface areas (rather than subsystem volumes), ground states are area-law entangled. For physical models of quantum matter, which have well-defined specific heat capacities (and are not necessarily FF), our bounds provide a way to convert this thermodynamic data into constraints on pure-state entanglement at both subextensive and extensive energies. We also show that our general upper bounds on half-system entanglement entropies are optimal, up to subleading corrections, in systems with reflection symmetry and above a subextensive energy threshold. A key application of our results is to constrain the entanglement of quantum states relevant to simulations of zero-temperature response functions, which have energies of order unity. We prove that, in wide varieties of FF systems in two dimensions and higher, the contributions of excitations to von Neumann entanglement entropy are subleading compared with the contribution from the ground state.
item.dc:creator: Samuel J. Garratt, Dmitry A. Abanin

item.title: Tame the Umklapp Processes in Real-Time Lattice Simulation for Hydrodynamics: An Ising Field Theory Study
item.description: arXiv:2606.09984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We calculate the real-time symmetric correlation function of the stress-energy tensor for a near-integrable Ising field theory consisting of three stable scalar particles via lattice Hamiltonian simulation. Using classical exact diagonalization and the matrix product state tensor network methods, we find that in the scaling region of the lattice theory, Umklapp processes that break continuum momentum conservation are suppressed and the sound modes of relativistic hydrodynamics emerge at long wavelength and late time in non-equilibrium dynamics. The extracted ratio of bulk viscosity to entropy density is $\zeta/s=3.06\pm 0.68$ and the speed of sound is $c_s/c=0.76 \pm 0.02$ at the temperature $T\approx 7.14$ in units of the lowest stable particle's mass. Our study demonstrates the utility of real-time lattice Hamiltonian simulation for describing hydrodynamization and calculating transport coefficients nonperturbatively.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Yao

item.title: Real-space spectral functions of three-dimensional billion-size topological non-Hermitian matter with tensor networks
item.description: arXiv:2606.16424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-Hermitian systems host unconventional topological phenomena, while real-space spectral calculations in three dimensions remain computationally challenging. Here, we develop a tensor-network framework that combines a quantics-based matrix-product-operator representation of large real-space tight-binding Hamiltonians with a non-Hermitian kernel polynomial method. The Hermitized spectral problem is retained within the compact tensor-network representation, enabling real-space spectral function calculations for systems exceeding one billion lattice sites. Using this approach, we investigate a three-dimensional non-Hermitian higher-order topological insulator and resolve its corner-mode spectral response on a billion-site lattice, demonstrating the scalability and computational reach of the method. By tuning the gain--loss strength, we identify distinct in-gap corner-mode features in the weak- and strong-gain--loss regimes. Our results establish a scalable tensor-network framework for real-space spectral calculations in exceptionally large non-Hermitian lattice systems.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Sun, Jose L. Lado, Guangze Chen

item.title: Surface charges in a Rydberg atom-nanowaveguide hybrid quantum system
item.description: arXiv:2607.00513v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hybrid quantum platforms based on highly excited Rydberg atoms coupled to nanophotonics devices offer a promising route toward scalable quantum networks and integrated quantum technologies. However, the close proximity of Rydberg atoms to dielectric nanostructures makes these systems particularly susceptible to uncontrolled surface electric fields that can lead to a degradation of the excitation process. Here, we experimentally investigate Rydberg excitation of laser-cooled $^{87}$Rb atoms via the evanescent field of an optical nanofiber in the presence of fiber-guided red- and blue-detuned light fields as used to trap ground state atoms in fiber-based dipole traps. We observe a time evolution of the Rydberg excitation spectrum when both the dipole trapping fields are on and the additional spectral features that appear can be suppressed by applying an external oscillating electric field to the system, strongly indicating that surface charge accumulation is responsible for the observed spectral feature. The experimental results are reproduced qualitatively by a model that incorporates DC energy level shifts arising from electric fields generated by charges deposited on the nanofiber surface. We identify Rydberg-ground state collisional ionization, which is enhanced by the dipole trapping fields, as the dominant mechanism for charge generation. These results provide new insight into charge dynamics at dielectric nanophotonic interfaces and establish practical guidelines for mitigating surface charge-induced electric fields in fiber-integrated Rydberg quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Aswathy Raj, Anna Kortel, Krishna Jadeja, Dylan J. Brown, Alexey Vylegzhanin, Robert L\"ow, S\'ile Nic Chormaic

item.title: Fourier imaging of collective spontaneous emission modes in superradiant cold atomic clouds
item.description: arXiv:2607.08421v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We measure the spatial pattern associated with the superradiant emission from a cloud of cold 87Rb atoms using Fourier imaging. We observe a highly directional, ring-shaped emission structure, which corresponds to a single collective jump operator associated to the most superradiant mode of the ensemble. Using spatial filtering, we isolate this channel and find the typical superradiant burst with superlinear scaling of the intensity with atom number. We compare our results to two models that describe the competition between the various decay channels, finding good agreement. Our work shows that the collective jump operators introduced by Carmichael et al. [Optics Communications 179, 417 (2000)] can be measured and manipulated.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Gavalda, Guillaume Tremblier, Martin Poitrinal, Sara Pancaldi, Antoine Browaeys, Igor Ferrier-Barbut

item.title: A robust and modular cesium magneto-optical trap using divergent laser beams
item.description: arXiv:2607.13145v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs) are a workhorse technology for neutral-atom quantum sensing, simulation, and computing. Here, we demonstrate a MOT optimized for inertial quantum sensing and precision metrology applications. Our MOT traps $4\times10^8$ cesium (Cs) atoms in a robust, modular system that achieves stable operation through two design features: (1) we use divergent cooling laser beams to reduce unwanted reflections and (2) optical elements are mounted in a fiber-coupled, compact, and modular cage rigidly attached to the vacuum chamber. Following polarization-gradient cooling (PGC), the system produces atom samples with temperatures below 10 ${\mu}$K, similar to those achieved in conventional MOTs that use collimated laser beams. In addition, we observe trapping of $2\times10^7$ Cs atoms in a non-conventional MOT geometry, where the cooling laser beams are diagonal to the principal axis of the quadrupole magnetic field.
item.dc:creator: Paola Luna, Kenneth Nakasone, Andrei Zhukov, Philip Wondrak, Brian P. Anderson, Benjamin F. Kanzer, Cristian D. Panda

item.title: HybridQC: Hardware-Grounded Simulation of Tightly Integrated Hybrid Quantum-Classical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.13352v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical performance depends on how quantum processors share classical compute, controllers, memory, and communication links. Circuit simulators and provider measurements expose kernel and job behavior, but leave topology-level questions about controller bottlenecks, quantum capacity, and mixed-workload contention unanswered. We present HybridQC, a discrete-event simulator for configurable hybrid compute units (HCUs). Users specify resource graphs containing classical compute, memory, controllers, quantum annealing (QA) and digital quantum computing (DQC) devices, and links. Jobs become dependent stages for preparation, quantum execution, transfers, reconstruction, and postprocessing. Finite capacities and selectable scheduling policies determine where stages wait and overlap. Service profiles use measurements from D-Wave Advantage 1 and Advantage 2 and IBM Kingston, Marrakesh, and Fez, separating physical quantum-processor occupancy from cloud wall time. Mean absolute percentage errors are 3.92%-8.04% for D-Wave access time and 5.26%-19.01% for IBM quantum seconds. Balanced 10x HCU scaling improves makespan by 2.19x-3.42x, while policy choice changes makespan by 1.80x for a mixed workload with 20 jobs per workload family. Scaling depends on which inputs grow: 100x data growth yields median runtime near 306 s, while 100x joint growth in circuits, shots, and depth reaches 4.806 x 10^7 s on the fixed HCU. HybridQC enables designers to study topology, scheduling, and workload growth before tightly integrated quantum-classical machines exist physically.
item.dc:creator: Panayiotis Christou, Shuwen Kan, Ying Mao

item.title: Spin-Resolved Decay of Axion-Like Particles into Electron--Positron Pairs in Strong Electromagnetic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.14558v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate spin-resolved decay of an axion-like particle (ALP) into an electron--positron pair in an intense laser field. Using the Baier--Katkov quasiclassical operator formalism in a constant crossed field, we derive a compact analytic rate retaining finite ALP-mass effects and the lepton spin degrees of freedom. In the massless limit, the spin-summed rate has the same weak- and strong-field asymptotic scalings as the corresponding photon-induced pair-creation rate, while the pseudoscalar coupling induces distinct spin-resolved channels and spin correlations. A finite ALP mass reorganizes the spectrum across the vacuum threshold, producing purely field-induced pair creation below threshold and spin-dependent oscillatory modulations above threshold through the coherent interplay of vacuum and field-assisted contributions. The entanglement of the produced pair reflects the dominant pair-creation mechanism. After the emission angles have been traced out, the reduced spin state near the vacuum threshold in weak fields is nearly maximally entangled and singlet-like. In the strong-field regime, it becomes triplet-like while retaining a concurrence approaching 1/2, whereas deep in the vacuum-dominated above-threshold regime it becomes triplet-like and separable. These results establish spin-resolved spectra and entanglement as characteristic signatures of finite-mass and threshold effects in strong-field ALP decay.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodan Mao, Yue-Yue Chen, Pei-Lun He

item.title: Reasoning about Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems
item.description: arXiv:2607.23137v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) is a computing paradigm in which measurements yield values over a continuous domain. CVQC is both a convenient computational framework for modeling physical quantum systems, and a good abstraction for hardware platforms based on quantum optics. Yet, the semantic foundations of CVQC remain underdeveloped. To address this gap, we develop a formal semantics for a core CV quantum programming language, and sound verification methods for program correctness. A main contribution of this work is to isolate a well-behaved quantitative predicate domain that achieves sufficient expressiveness to accommodate unbounded values as they arise in the infinite-dimensional, continuous setting. Specifically, we choose closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, representing finite expectations, domains of finiteness, and infinite penalties in one ordered object. We validate our choice by establishing that our semantic predicates satisfy desirable closure properties including the definition of weakest preconditions. We validate our design with two case studies, including an example based on the celebrated GKP error-correcting code, for which we establish a second moment bound.
item.dc:creator: Tianshi Yu, Gilles Barthe, Minbo Gao, Mingsheng Ying, Li Zhou

item.title: Phase-Drift Limits and Adaptive Quadrature Readout in Programmable Photonic Processors
item.description: arXiv:2608.02249v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Phase fluctuations between optical inputs limit programmable photonic processors because their output powers depend on coherent interference. We study the phase-drift penalty that arises when sine and cosine quadratures are measured sequentially rather than simultaneously. The analysis is motivated by measurements from an eight-mode programmable photonic processor, including 35 free-running recordings of 300 s acquired at approximately 125 samples per second per channel. These recordings provide an empirical route for estimating the phase-increment variance at a selected reconfiguration interval. The estimate is defined at the time of the second measurement. For fixed quadrature order, perturbation of the atan2 reconstruction gives $e_{C\to S}=-\delta_\tau\sin^2\phi_0+O(\delta_\tau^2)$ and $e_{S\to C}=-\delta_\tau\cos^2\phi_0+O(\delta_\tau^2)$. Writing $Q_\tau=\operatorname{Var}(\delta_\tau)$, uniform phase averaging gives the first-order drift mean-square error $3Q_\tau/8$. A phase-predicted ordering rule measures the locally less informative quadrature first and the more informative quadrature second. Its uniform first-order penalty is $(3/8-1/\pi)Q_\tau$, which is 84.9 percent below the fixed-order value. We also derive an increment-aware estimator from a local state-space model. Marginalizing the unknown phase increment increases the variance of a stale phase observation by $Q_\tau$, reducing its Fisher information from $I$ to $I/(1+IQ_\tau)$. For ideal balanced Poisson detection, the Fisher information of each quadrature equals its detected signal-photon number. This yields dimensionless architecture boundaries in spatial information and phase-increment variance. Nonlinear Monte Carlo simulations validate the perturbative laws, quantify robustness to prediction error, and compare simultaneous, fixed-order, increment-aware, and adaptive receivers under a common noise model.
item.dc:creator: G\"okhan Elmas, Igor A. Litvin, Janis N\"otzel

item.title: Magneto-oscillations, nonlinearity, and nonreciprocity of Coulomb drag in quantum circuits
item.description: arXiv:2608.02812v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of Coulomb drag in interactively coupled quantum circuits built of adiabatic constrictions: quantum point contacts and short quantum-wire channels. The interplay of spatial confinement and magnetic field leads to a rich oscillatory response of the drag current as a function of gate voltage and magnetic field: drag peaks track the depopulation of magnetoelectric subbands, are asymptotically periodic in inverse field, and their visibility is controlled by the competition of temperature with the field-sharpened tunneling width of the constriction. We derive a closed expression for the linear drag conductance whose interaction kernel simplifies dramatically in the experimentally relevant limit of a long thermal length compared with the range of the interwire coupling, investigate the drag in the nonlinear regime, where the drag current measures the transconductance of the drive channel at any field, and discuss physically motivated models of dissipation-induced nonreciprocity of the drag signal. Extensions accounting for Zeeman splitting, interaction renormalization of the barrier transmission, backscattering at high field, and the frequency structure of the circuit coupling delineate how each mechanism imprints itself on the temperature dependence and lineshapes of the drag oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Alex Levchenko, Mingyang Zheng, Dominique Laroche

item.title: On the quantum communication complexity of total functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.18784v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a total function with a polylogarithmic two-message quantum protocol, whereas every randomised protocol, even with arbitrarily many rounds, requires polynomial communication.
item.dc:creator: Dmytro Gavinsky

item.title: Quantized Mereology
item.description: arXiv:2609.01620v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates quantized mereology, which merges quantum information theory with classical mereology, the formal analysis of the part-whole relationship. It emphasizes that information about crisp mereological relations is captured by classical bits, whereas mereological vagueness involves the use of quantum bits, or qubits, to capture mereological information. Transitioning from classical bits to qubits offers a new understanding of part-whole relations among entities that are subject to mereological vagueness. This paper methodically studies the quantized mereology that arises from the classical RCC5 formalism, one of the most widely studied formalisms in Qualitative Reasoning (QR), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence. The argument is made that this method can be extended to quantize more sophisticated QR formalisms, mirroring how strategies are used in physics to transition from classical to quantum systems. The study explores: (i) the conversion of bits to qubits while understanding that these (qu)bits convey mereological information; (ii) the representation of qubit states via set partitions, acknowledging that set theory aligns more closely with classical logic than with the complex vector spaces employed in quantum physics; (iii) demonstrating that classical QR formalisms can be seen as special cases within quantized formalisms; and (iv) showing that qubits more effectively encapsulate information about vague phenomena.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 87, Article 12 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Thomas Bittner

item.title: Sparse Walsh-Pauli Correlation Encoding for MaxCut: A Quantum-Inspired Formulation with Quantum-Hardware Validation
item.description: arXiv:2609.08907v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a sparse Walsh-Pauli correlation encoding for MaxCut, in which graph variables are represented by diagonal Pauli-string expectation values computed classically as normalized XOR autocorrelations of Walsh coefficients. The complete Walsh basis can reproduce the diagonal correlators of arbitrary quantum states, while a structured sparse support reduces the number of trainable coefficients to $m+1$ for $m$ graph variables. We evaluate the method on $1{,}400$ held-out random graphs with up to $7{,}000$ vertices, obtaining empirical approximation ratios near $0.98$ relative to MQLib heuristic references. On Gset instances G14, G23, G60, and G64, the sparse model achieves mean refined approximation ratios of $0.9828$, $0.9926$, $0.9781$, and $0.9369$, respectively, with $80.4\%$-$89.3\%$ fewer parameters than the complete Walsh representation. The trained coefficients are transferred without retraining to quantum circuits. Statevector simulations of the four Gset instances achieve fidelities above $0.99994$ and preserve all correlator signs. Separately, a seven-qubit experiment on a $15$-vertex graph executed on IBM quantum hardware achieves a correlator-sign agreement of $0.927\pm0.049$ relative to the corresponding noiseless circuit. These results demonstrate the potential of sparse Walsh-PCE for large-instance quantum-inspired MaxCut optimization while validating the transfer of classically trained parameters to quantum hardware.
item.dc:creator: Cesar Augusto do Amaral, Nicol\'as Legnazzi, Marcos Vinicius Reballo, Marcus Ritt, Alexsandro Santos da Rosa J\'unior, Fernando Augusto Caletti de Barros

item.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
item.description: arXiv:2609.24295v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match: worth only a factor 1.15. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a further 2.7. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV- spin coherence rather than shortening it.

item.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.10682v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study symmetric gapped ground states of one-dimensional spin $S$ chains with a continuous exponential symmetry $U(1)\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with integer base $q$, where the U(1) charge has a modulated unit of charge $q^{L-j}$ decaying exponentially with site $j$. The simplest model is a quantum breakdown model that can be viewed as a $q$-deformation of the XXZ Haldane spin chain. We show that the topology of their symmetric ground states crucially depends on $S$ and $q$. For integer $S$, odd $q$ allows a nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ Haldane-type symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase with protected edge modes, while even $q$ allows no nontrivial SPT phase. For half-odd integer $S$, odd $q$ prohibits any unique symmetric gapped ground state due to a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis obstruction, whereas even $q$ enforces a novel symmetric gapped phase which we name as the ``half-SPT" phase. Unconventionally, the half-SPT phase only has a symmetry protected edge mode on one edge, and has half of the string orders of an SPT phase. Our results uncover a new type of symmetry-protected gapped phases beyond existing classification schemes.

item.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.13246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.
